newsitem.title: CHINA: Matahari US$100 mln FRN postponed.
newsitem.headline: Matahari US$100 mln FRN postponed.

text.p: PT Matahari Putra Prima's US$100 million floating-rate note issue has been shelved until market conditions improve, bankers said on Tuesday.
"It's simply been postponed until market conditions improve," said a banker close to the deal, adding that Matahari did not have immediate need of the money.
"So it doesn't really make sense to go out into the market, where there's a lot of uncertainty (and) they may end up having to pay a premium," he said.
He said the deal would be relaunched when market conditions improved, without giving a specific date.
The Matahari Putra Prima deal was being arranged by BT Asia and Bear Stearns Asia.
Pricing was not announced, but it was expected to pay a coupon of 210 basis points over the six-month London interbank offered rate, and there were no put or call options.
Bankers said recent attacks on Asian currencies have deterred some issuers, partly because the attacks have forced up interest rates paid by issuers from Asia.
They said issuers who did not immediately need cash planned to wait until rates fell, and currencies were less volatile, making a currency swap easier to work out.
